prompt_text: I want to try a tanning salon in Tyler. Which specific salons should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: What is the best tanning salon in Tyler TX?
answer_verbatim:
Quick question before I give specific names: do you mean Tyler, Texas? And are you looking for UV tanning (beds/booths) or a sunless spray tan? I can either (A) give a short list of actual salons in Tyler with phone numbers and reasons to call (if you confirm location), or (B) give a prioritized list of the types of places you should call plus an exact script of what to ask so you can compare them yourself.

If you want me to pick actual salons, tell me:
- Confirm “Tyler, TX” (or give the ZIP or a different Tyler)
- UV tanning or spray tan (or either)

If you’d rather decide now, here’s what you should call and why — plus exactly what to ask.

Which places to call (general categories) and why
- National chains (e.g., Palm Beach Tan / Sun Tan City-type locations)
  - Why: consistent equipment and training, clear membership options, multiple locations/hours.
- Local boutique spray-tan studios or medi-spas
  - Why: usually better custom airbrush results, experienced artists, higher-quality solutions and color matching.
- Full-service tanning salons with both UV beds and spray booths
  - Why: flexible options if you want both UV and sunless in one place.
- Gyms or beauty salons that offer tanning
  - Why: convenient if you want a one-stop trip (workout + tan) or cheaper add-on pricing.
- Dermatology / medical spas (for professional advice)
  - Why: safest if you have sensitive skin, history of skin cancer, meds that increase sun sensitivity, or want medical-grade spray/tanning advice.

What to ask when you call (use this exact script)
1. “What tanning services do you offer — UV beds, stand-up booths, spray tan (airbrush or booth)?”
2. If UV: “What types of beds do you have (high-pressure vs low-pressure/frequency), how old are the bulbs, and how often are the beds serviced/cleaned?”
3. If spray: “Is the spray tan technician-trained/airbrush or automatic booth? What solution brand do you use? Do you offer a patch test or sample photos?”
4. “Do you require an appointment for first-timers? Do you offer a consultation to pick the best level for my skin tone?”
5. “What are prices for a single session, and what are membership or package options? Any hidden fees (start-up cap, lotion, expiration dates)?”
6. “What are your sanitation practices between customers? Do you provide eye protection, disposable footwear, towels?”
7. “Do you have age restrictions or require parent consent for minors?”
8. “Do you offer any tan guarantees or corrective services if the color comes out uneven?”
9. “What COVID/safety policies should I know about?” (if relevant)
10. “Do you have before/after photos or online reviews I can look at?”

How to compare answers
- Prefer recent bulbs/high-pressure beds for faster, more even UV tans (if you go UV).
- For spray, prefer a trained technician who does airbrush or a proven solution brand (read reviews).
- Cleanliness and clear sanitation answers are a must.
- Good salons will offer a consult for first timers and explain prep/care.
- Compare total per-visit cost plus what you’ll need to buy (lotions, eyewear).
- Check online reviews and photos after calling.

Safety notes (short)
- UV tanning increases skin-cancer risk; limit frequency, follow staff guidance, and use eye protection.
- Spray tans are safer for color without UV exposure — ask about ingredients if you have allergies.
- If you have fair skin, medical issues, a history of skin cancer, or take photosensitizing meds, consult a dermatologist before UV tanning.

If you want, I’ll now look up 4–6 specific salons in Tyler, TX (with phone numbers, addresses, and a one-line reason to call each). Just confirm you mean Tyler, TX and whether you prefer UV or spray.
